executiveSummary: GM1695's 2025 identity, contained reference point, 8,046-resident control, fourteen neighbourhoods, six BAG places, ten BRT settlements and three logical road-border links are internally coherent; all ten canonical presets also execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services. One Kats BAG label point lies just outside the independently generalized CBS boundary and is a geometry/edition caveat, not proof that Kats is outside the municipality. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Noord-Beveland is a defended low-lying polder island between Oosterschelde and Veerse Meer whose primary access is structured by N256 over Zandkreekdam toward Goes and Zeelandbrug toward Schouwen-Duiveland, plus N57 over Veerse Gatdam toward Veere. The municipal vision explicitly says part of N256 is among the first areas to inundate and that suitable high-water refuge sites were not yet available; a current provincial programme still treats evacuation-road capacity and shelter identification as work in progress. The simulator instead reports an unselected major-river depth of 0.689921 at T+24 and T+72, no affected residents and 37,118 rising to 152,126 person-hours, although the canonical Rhine/Meuse/IJssel source has no direct local pathway. The locally relevant coastal preset reports exact depth 2.277241, only 412 affected residents and 94,038 person-hours at T+24, then zero depth and affected residents at T+72 while burden reaches 298,679, without a tide/surge, Oosterscheldekering, named defence, breach/overtopping, connected polder, arrival, duration, recession or pump state. That resident-only denominator is especially unsafe operationally: the municipality's 2025 tourism policy records 33,310 sleeping places and 2,351,200 overnight stays in 2023, while its adopted vision reports summer presence around 50,000 people. Seasonal visitors, marina/boat users and day visitors are absent. Pluvial and severe-storm residual depths likewise ignore polder catchments, receiving levels, sewers and pumps. Nine active hazard/component families reuse one fourteen-neighbourhood seed. A controlled ignition in Recreatiegebied Kamperland creates city flame 0.316427 and smoke 0.415641 but zero affected residents and no source-contained consequence. Public context exposes forty-nine partial water/wastewater objects, two Zandkreek observations, four Zandkreeksluis forecasts through T+24, one Stedin capacity-planning sample, 31 antenna sites and five education locations. These do not publish live connectivity, capacity compatibility, backup, staffing, stock, outage or restoration. Exact first-72-hour services, route access, evacuation, care and recovery must remain visibly synthetic or Unknown until event-specific coastal/pluvial/fire forcing, defence and polder state, dynamic population, crossing status, external hospital acceptance and an accountable action/resource ledger are bound; missing public data is never zero, safe, open or recovered.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1695 official 2025 identity, neighbourhood, place and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipality and regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: Annual CBS/PDOK inputs identify GM1695 as Noord-Beveland in Zeeland and Veiligheidsregio Zeeland, with 8,046 residents, density 94/km², 30.5% aged 65 or older and 1,513 one-person households. The reference point [3.7681716891428554,51.57746755261654] lies inside the generalized 2025 boundary.

Fourteen neighbourhoods in six districts sum to 8,045 residents, one below the municipal control (-0.012%); published households total 3,995 and rounded age-65-plus rows total 2,455. Deterministic allocation adds one resident without rewriting observations.

Colijnsplaat, Geersdijk, Kamperland, Kats, Kortgene and Wissenkerke are the six BAG places. Ten BRT features comprise two buurtschappen, two gehuchten and six woonkernen; neither dataset supplies emergency roles or dynamic occupancy.

The Kats BAG label point falls outside the independently generalized CBS polygon. This coastal-edge mismatch requires full-resolution/edition review and must not be interpreted as exclusion from the municipality.

District-heating and public-charging fields are null in all fourteen neighbourhoods; average home value has two null rows and cars-per-household four. Null remains NoData, not numeric zero or service absence.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Omgevingsvisie Noord-Beveland 2030
evidenceSources.edition: Adopted by the municipal council 16 December 2021; ten-year planning/context record; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The vision describes a polder island between Oosterschelde and Veerse Meer, with historic creeks/low areas, little or no freshwater-lens formation, salinisation, limited infiltration and climate stress from intense rain, prolonged wetness, drought, heat and flood consequences.

Although its 2016 stress test called Noord-Beveland the safest island in the Zeeuwse Delta, the same vision says preventive measures have limits and the municipality was insufficiently prepared for extremes. Planning language is not a current safety guarantee.

The authority says part of the principal N256 through-road is among the first areas to inundate and that no suitable high-water refuge sites were available. Raising N256, identifying safe-shelter search areas and fitting doors to openings such as bicycle tunnels require further work.

The vision identifies ageing, youth departure and large tourist numbers as increasing acute-care demand; summer presence can rise to about 50,000 people. This is seasonal planning context, not an event-time population count.
The municipality asks Zeeland to treat Deltaweg/N256 as an important emergency route and separately identifies nature-fire separation between nature and recreation areas.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Visie duurzame recreatie en toerisme Noord-Beveland
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal policy PDF published February 2025; underlying accommodation/overnight-stay reference year 2023; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The policy lists 9,080 accommodation/berth units and 33,310 sleeping places in 2023, including 9,050 tourist camping places, 8,480 privately owned holiday-home/chalet/apartment/room places, 7,740 annual-pitch places and 4,310 commercially rented holiday-unit places.

It reports 2,351,200 overnight stays in 2023 and states visitors add pressure to roads and general practitioners. Sleeping-place capacity is not actual occupancy; overnight stays do not identify who is present at an incident checkpoint.

Residents, registered overnight guests, fixed guests, day visitors, marina/boat users, workers and responders require separate timestamped populations. None may be substituted by the 8,046 resident denominator or by maximum bed capacity.
The document is a tourism policy and inventory, not an evacuation registration, emergency-contact feed, support-site list or T+72 occupancy forecast.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Noord-Beveland freshwater and salinity monitoring context
evidenceSources.edition: Current water-board page inspected 3 September 2026; monitoring/project context; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: Noord-Beveland, Zeeland, Scheldestromen and twenty farmers established the two-year 'Boeren meten water' project to improve knowledge of salinity in the surface-water system.

Participants measure electrical conductivity every two weeks at locations chosen with the water board; data are collected in a dashboard and linked to the board's system. Sampling remains point/project evidence, not a continuous live freshwater-volume or drinking-water-quality surface.

The project exists because robust freshwater conditions and salinisation remain knowledge/action issues. Missing measurements or a normal point never mean adequate island-wide supply or no drought impact.
Agricultural freshwater, polder level management, wastewater and Evides drinking water are distinct chains and must not share one generic Water availability value.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Deltaweg/Zeelandbrug, N57/Veerse Gatdam and Zandkreekdam/sluis lifecycle context
evidenceSources.edition: Provincial Zeelandbrug renovation notice for autumn 2026; RWS Zandkreeksluis project 2023–2028 and N57 current planning inspected 3 September 2026; source-specific public-page reuse terms not stated
supports: N256 is one physical north–south Deltaweg corridor: south via Zandkreekdam to Goes/A58 and north via Zeelandbrug to Schouwen-Duiveland. N57 crosses Veerse Gatdam to Veere/Walcheren and multiple Delta Works farther north.

The province planned a Zeelandbrug bascule renovation and full-deck surfacing in the 1 September–31 December 2026 window, with up to eight weeks of closure, but the notice does not confirm an exact start or live status on the audit date. Lifecycle planning is not a closure observation.

RWS records the 2023–2028 Zandkreeksluis project, two road bridges at the complex and scheduled door work. Construction dates/availability differ for road and shipping modes and must retain issue, start, end, mode and completion confirmation.

Current RWS planning includes an N57 closure between Banjaard and Serooskerke on 9–10 September 2026. It is future context at the 3 September audit time, not an active closure and not a generic hazard effect.
NWB geometry and nominal value 150 do not establish lanes, vehicles/hour, evacuation throughput, emergency access, detour capacity or simultaneous operability of the island's three boundary links.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Regionaal Crisisplan 2026–2029 and Zeeland climate-adaptation execution agenda
evidenceSources.edition: Regional crisis plan effective 3 January 2026; provincial climate-adaptation agenda progress record inspected 3 September 2026; legal/planning evidence
supports: The current crisis plan targets first CoPI within 30 minutes, ROT within 45 minutes and GBT/RBT within 60 minutes after large-scale alerting, plus continuous command and handover into the recovery phase. Targets are doctrine, not proof of incident-time arrival, staffing or resources.

Because of Zeeland geography, the plan explicitly says the 30-minute CoPI norm cannot always be met outside focus areas; Noord-Beveland is in the northern duty area. This uncertainty must be preserved in response-time assumptions.

Public-care processes include moving, receiving and caring for people and arranging food, drinking water, clothing, money, medicine, temporary housing and measures during utility/gas/telecom failure. They define responsibilities, not activated sites, quantities or completion.

The provincial agenda says evacuation depends on road capacity, evacuee numbers and available transport. A Zeeland-wide crisis-road study is underway, while use of new objects for reception/shelter was marked not yet being implemented.
A doctrine milestone cannot directly change model service availability or count as a completed action without incident, actor, resource, place, valid time and confirmation.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Dutch water boards and Rijkswaterstaat
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Partial water/wastewater register and timestamped Zandkreek observations/forecasts
evidenceSources.edition: HWH deployment snapshot retrieved 2026-09-03T01:38:15Z, CC BY-SA 4.0 with variable contributor completeness; Waterinfo observations retrieved 2026-09-02T18:03:18Z and forecasts 2026-09-03T04:29:19Z, CC0 unless component exception
supports: Full-resolution containment assigns forty-nine HWH points to GM1695: seven sewer pumps, one wastewater-treatment plant, eleven surface-water pumps, one sluice and twenty-nine weirs. Seven sewer and eight surface-water pumps have non-null capacity numbers; units/connectivity and live achievable flow remain source-specific or unresolved.

Named context includes rwzi Camperlandpolder, Gemaal Jacoba, De Valle, Willem, Adriaan and Uitwateringssluis de Valle. 'Gerealiseerd' and register presence mean lifecycle/existence, not current control, power/backup or operability.
Two local observations at 2026-09-02T17:30Z report 120.75 m³/s at Kats Zandkreekdam and -3 cm NAP at Zandkreeksluis kolk 1. They are point/time values, not surge, defence, polder or route state.

Four Zandkreeksluis water-level forecast points provide T+1/+6/+12/+24 values of 160/-3/97/54 cm NAP. No local T+48 or T+72 forecast point was returned; point guidance is not an inundation surface or operating instruction, and absent horizons remain NoData.

evidenceSources.publisher: Stichting Mijn Aansluiting, Stedin, Evides, Netbeheer Nederland, RDI, DUO and RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Island utility responsibility, planning, telecom, education and external acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Public provider query and deployment snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026; provider polygons last updated per discipline 17 December 2025–12 May 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026, CC0; source-specific licences/cadences
supports: The reference-point query returns Stedin for electricity and gas and Evides for drinking water, but no drainage or media polygon. Public Domain polygons are responsibility context, not address connectivity, physical topology, outage, pressure, coverage quality or restoration.

One postcode sample 4491GB maps to Stedin area Goes de Poel and reports null existing/required withdrawal/injection, a 38.1 MW withdrawal queue across thirteen requests, eight projects and earliest 2030. Null remains Unknown and the sample is planning context, not municipal capacity or current reserve.
RDI assigns 31 sites/69 antennas and DUO five education locations; registers do not establish coverage, backhaul, power/backup, occupancy, shelter designation, stock or staffing.

No RIVM acute-care point lies inside. Admiraal De Ruyter Ziekenhuis in Goes is about 14.1 km straight-line from the reference point and its annual 24/7 emergency/room/visit record does not establish N256 access, ambulance availability, live staffing, backup, diversion or acceptance.

The deployment assigns zero local fixed KNMI weather observations/warnings, RIVM PM2.5 stations, government-service points, NDW situations and 365-day seismic origins. Each is scoped NoData, never normal weather/air, open roads, service availability or safety.

identity.summary: GM1695, Noord-Beveland, Zeeland and Veiligheidsregio Zeeland agree across generated and official 2025 sources.
notes: Feature ID, bundle code/name, province and safety-region membership are coherent.
The municipality reference point lies inside the generalized 2025 geometry.
Administrative edition, planning/lifecycle, timestamped observation/forecast and synthetic exercise time remain separate.

geography.summary: Island context is strong, but generalized coastal geometry and missing defence/polder connectivity prevent hydraulic use.
notes: The Kats BAG centre mismatch demonstrates that independently generalized/dated boundaries must not be used as exact coastal containment.
Oosterschelde, Veerse Meer, sea defences, historic polders/creeks, fresh/salt water and rainfall drainage are distinct mechanisms.
Use full-resolution official boundaries for joins and authority hydraulic geometry for consequence modelling.

demography.summary: Resident population reconciles, but seasonal exposure can greatly exceed the resident control and is absent from the model.
notes: Published neighbourhood population is 8,045, one below the 8,046 control (-0.012%); deterministic reconciliation adds one resident.
The authority reports 33,310 sleeping places, 2,351,200 annual overnight stays in 2023 and summer presence around 50,000 in the adopted vision.
Bed capacity, annual nights and planning peak are not live occupancy; each visitor/worker/marina/respondent population requires time and source.

regionalDetail.summary: All fourteen neighbourhoods are retained, but partial statistics and resident-weighted source-blind allocation omit coastal/recreation dynamics.
notes: Kamperland, Kortgene-Dorp, Colijnsplaat and Wissenkerke dominate resident totals, but resident size is not coastal, pluvial, wind or visitor exposure.
Recreatiegebied Kamperland has only 200 registered residents and cannot proxy its seasonal occupancy.
District heating/charging and partial household-value/car data remain NoData.

settlements.summary: Six BAG places and ten BRT settlements preserve village context, subject to the Kats generalized-boundary caveat.
notes: The ten BRT types are two buurtschappen, two gehuchten and six woonkernen.
The Kats label-point mismatch requires geometry review, not deletion or reassignment.
A village, holiday park, school, marina or campsite is not a confirmed refuge/support site; E02/E06 explicitly show shelter planning is incomplete.

transport.summary: The three boundary links are island chokepoints whose physical structures, common causes, dates and evacuation/care roles are not represented.
notes: The two N256 edges are series segments of one Deltaweg corridor over Zandkreekdam and Zeelandbrug and must never add as independent capacity.
N57 over Veerse Gatdam is a third boundary route but not proof of an independent usable evacuation/care path during surge, wind, closure or congestion.
No local rail station exists; fourteen GTFS stop areas are schedules, not bus/driver/route continuity. External acute care in Goes depends materially on N256/Zandkreek access.

emergencyContext.summary: Current doctrine and municipal planning define actions and gaps, but no selected incident or complete T0–T+72 resource state exists.
notes: CoPI/ROT/GBT/RBT times are organizational targets; Zeeland geography means the 30-minute CoPI norm is not always achievable.
N256 raising, refuge-site identification and Zeeland-wide evacuation roads remain planning/action items, not completed incident capacity.
Evacuee counts, transport, shelter openings/capacity, support stocks, responders, care acceptance, fuel and restoration remain Unknown.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets execute at six checkpoints across all eight services for GM1695.
notes: Initial focused audit:model passed one file/two tests in 30.34 seconds, tests 30.11 seconds.
Diagnostic all-preset run passed one file/two tests in 13.93 seconds, tests 13.71 seconds; controlled Recreatiegebied Kamperland ignition executed in 0.394 seconds.
Final focused audit:model passed one file/two tests in 47.69 seconds, tests 47.27 seconds.
Execution coverage is not physical, spatial, population, network, operational or recovery calibration.

numericalInvariants.summary: Bounds, resident/demand/delivery reconciliation, determinism and cumulative-burden invariants hold for the resident-only model.
notes: All numeric outputs are finite and bounded; affected population is integral and no greater than the fixed resident control 8,046.
Neighbourhood residents and service demand/delivery sums reconcile at every tested frame.
The invariant itself exposes the seasonal limitation: visitors cannot be affected because they are absent from both denominator and spatial allocation.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A common seeded fourteen-neighbourhood surface replaces defence/polder, rainfall, visitor, fire, wind, heat and cyber geography.
notes: Nine active preset/component families reuse one local hash rather than sampling mechanism-specific footprints.
Coastal affected counts mostly follow resident population and ignore dynamic accommodation/marina exposure, defences, polders and route inundation.
Controlled fire in Recreatiegebied Kamperland produces flame 0.316427 and smoke 0.415641 but zero affected residents everywhere; source containment and visitor exposure both fail.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact service availability omits island crossings, polder/freshwater/wastewater chains, external care and operator state.
notes: Forty-nine HWH assets and six Waterinfo records remain display context and do not drive catchment, gate/pump/sluice, receiving level, salinity, power/backup or dewatering.
Logical NWB balancing does not represent bridge/dam failure, weather/maintenance closure, congestion, evacuation direction, bus continuity or Adrz route/acceptance.
Provider polygons, one planning sample, antennas/schools and an external annual hospital record do not calibrate live availability, capacity, backup or restoration.

causalTrace.summary: Arithmetic ledgers reconcile, but mechanism, dynamic-population and operational provenance do not support displayed precision.
notes: Hazard/service contribution sums and counterfactual records remain inspectable.
At T+24 coastal output reports depth 2.277241, 412 resident affected and 94,038 person-hours; this is scenario arithmetic, not an authority forecast, selected defence failure or total people exposed.

The Groningen earthquake has zero local ground motion, severity and affected residents but still accumulates 185 person-hours at T+24 and 340 at T+72; that burden is an indirect synthetic network effect, not local earthquake damage.

recovery72h.summary: T+72 water disappearance, service recovery and cumulative burden are not driven by confirmed island actions/resources or a T+72 forecast.
notes: Coastal depth/affected change 2.277241/412→0/0 from T+24 to T+72 while burden grows 94,038→298,679 and Mobility rises 0.815693→0.914461; no drainage, crossing-clearance, evacuation or repair action causes this trajectory.
Compound depth remains 0.449164 while affected residents change 210→189 and burden 81,003→322,288; seven services freeze and Facilities changes 0.853202→0.866601 without governed action state.

Waterinfo local forecasts stop at T+24. No public record confirms T+72 defence/pump status, route clearance, shelter, visitor accountability, hospital acceptance, generators/fuel, water distribution, resupply or restoration.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, centre containment, regional membership and resident reconciliation are coherent.
findings.evidence: E01 plus audit:context verify GM1695/Noord-Beveland/Zeeland/VRZ, the contained reference point and a one-resident (-0.012%) neighbourhood rounding difference reconciled deterministically.
findings.action: Retain the 2025 edition, exact nulls, deterministic reconciliation and separate BAG/BRT semantics.

findings.summary: The Kats BAG label falls outside the generalized CBS boundary and prevents exact coastal-edge use.
findings.evidence: E01 shows one of six BAG centres outside the independently versioned/generalized polygon. Island shorelines, dams, polders and administrative generalization are not exact hydraulic boundaries.
findings.action: Retain Kats and the caveat; use full-resolution co-edition administrative geometry for joins and authority flood/polder geometry for consequences.

findings.summary: The canonical major-river preset creates a false direct source on Noord-Beveland.
findings.evidence: River T+24/T+72 reports depth 0.689921 and severity 0.216957 with zero affected residents but burden 37,118→152,126. E02/E04/E07 establish coastal/Veerse Meer/polder/salinity pathways, not a selected Rhine/Meuse/IJssel source.
findings.action: Suppress direct canonical major-river forcing for GM1695 and test exact narrow-source zero; preserve Oosterschelde, Veerse Meer, polder, backwater and indirect supply pathways as Unknown until selected.

findings.summary: Locally relevant coastal forcing has unsupported depth, exposure and complete hydraulic disappearance by T+72.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+24 reports depth 2.277241, 412 resident affected and 94,038 person-hours, then exact depth/affected zero at T+72 while burden reaches 298,679. No source selects tide/surge, Oosterscheldekering, defence, breach/overtopping, polder footprint, arrival, recession or pumping.
findings.action: Retain only visibly unsupported coastal context until a versioned RWS/Scheldestromen/LIWO event binds boundary/datum/time, named defence and state, failure mode, footprint, depth, population, duration, drainage and uncertainty.

findings.summary: One shared local seed and failed controlled-fire consequence replace mechanism-specific geography.
findings.evidence: Nine active families reuse one fourteen-neighbourhood hash. Moving ignition into Recreatiegebied Kamperland yields city flame 0.316427/smoke 0.415641 but zero affected residents, despite E02's nature/recreation separation concern and E03's dynamic visitors.
findings.action: Replace the shared seed with hazard-specific hydraulic, pluvial, wind, heat, fire/plume and cyber surfaces; require eligible fuel, source containment, valid-time weather, access/water and suppression state.

findings.summary: Resident-only exposure omits a seasonal population several times larger than the official resident control.
findings.evidence: E01 has 8,046 residents; E03 reports 33,310 sleeping places and 2,351,200 overnight stays in 2023; E02 reports summer presence around 50,000. The model invariant caps all affected output at 8,046 and allocates only registered residents.
findings.action: Add timestamped residents, registered guests, estimated unregistered/day/marina users, staff/responders and uncertainty as separate non-double-counted populations; never substitute beds or annual nights for live occupancy.

findings.summary: Rain, prolonged wetness, salinity and drought are collapsed into generic depth/Water values.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 has rain zero, depth 0.207954, affected zero and 22,058 person-hours; severe storm has residual depth 0.403407 after wind/rain zero. E02/E04 distinguish intense/prolonged rain, little freshwater lens, limited infiltration, salinisation and monitored surface water.
findings.action: Bind rain to AHN/BGT, Zeeland stress-test, polder/catchment, sewer/pump/outfall and receiving-level state; model agricultural freshwater/salinity separately from drinking water and keep unsampled conditions Unknown.

findings.summary: Partial water assets and Zandkreek points cannot support exact Water/Drainage performance or dewatering.
findings.evidence: E07 exposes 49 assets, fifteen non-null pump capacities, two observations and forecasts only through T+24. Register presence and point values establish neither connected catchments, compatible units, remaining capacity, control, backup nor T+72 operation.
findings.action: Integrate authority-reviewed catchments, flow direction, units, control/outfall/receiving level, sewer/WWTP, power/backup and valid-time aggregate state where publishable; otherwise affectsSimulation=false and Unknown.

findings.summary: Island access, evacuation and external acute care depend on unmodelled bridge/dam and N256 flood states.
findings.evidence: E02 says N256 can inundate first and suitable high-water refuge sites were absent; E05 shows lifecycle work/closures; E06 says evacuation depends on roads, people and vehicles. The two N256 logical edges are one series corridor, N57 is not guaranteed independent, and Adrz Goes is external via Zandkreek access.
findings.action: Model Zeelandbrug, Zandkreekdam/sluis bridges, Veerse Gatdam and low N256 sections as typed non-additive assets; bind direction/mode/time/closure, congestion, vehicle, shelter and hospital acceptance or leave route/care state Unknown.

findings.summary: Provider areas, one planning sample and facility registers cannot calibrate exact island utility availability.
findings.evidence: E08 identifies Stedin/Evides responsibility, no drainage/media polygon, one Goes de Poel planning sample with null current-capacity fields, 31 antenna sites and five schools but no connectivity, live load/pressure/quality/outage, backhaul, backup, staff, stock or repair state.
findings.action: Label percentages synthetic; ingest only authorised timestamped aggregate outage/restoration evidence, preserve topology/security constraints and never convert a no-match, null or sample into zero or municipal coverage.

findings.summary: Sparse observations, horizon gaps and narrow direct zeros need explicit scope labels.
findings.evidence: E07 stops local water forecasts at T+24; E08 has zero local fixed weather/warning, air, road-situation, government, acute-care and recent seismic points. Direct earthquake ground motion is zero while indirect burden persists; none implies normal conditions, open routes or all-hazard safety.
findings.action: Show location, issue/valid/expiry time, quality, units/datum, coverage and evidence class; distinguish modeled zero, NoData, Unknown, not applicable and indirect synthetic effect in maps/exports.

findings.summary: First-72-hour evacuation, service and recovery changes lack accountable local actions and resources.
findings.evidence: Coastal water disappears and Mobility recovers while burden triples; compound depth/services largely freeze. E06 defines crisis roles/targets but E02/E06 show route/shelter gaps, and no source confirms defence/pump switching, evacuation, visitor accountability, refuge, hospital acceptance, fuel, water, resupply or repair completion.
findings.action: Add a T0/6/12/24/48/72 incident/action/resource/blocker ledger with actor, proposal/request/confirmation/dispatch/active/completion, location, capacity, dependency, valid/expiry time and uncertainty; suppress unconfirmed recovery attribution.

corrections.summary: Suppress Noord-Beveland's false direct major-river signal and replace generic coastal/pluvial fields with selected defence–polder and rain–drainage events.
corrections.validation: Canonical Rhine/Meuse/IJssel direct forcing is exactly zero but not an all-clear; coastal/pluvial results require source event, boundary/datum, defence/control state, connected footprint, issue/valid time, duration/recession, uncertainty/licence and NoData.

corrections.summary: Add dynamic seasonal exposure without treating beds, annual nights or policy peak as live occupancy.
corrections.validation: Resident, registered-guest, estimated day/marina/worker and responder cohorts preserve source/time/uncertainty and avoid double counting; affected values reconcile per cohort and Unknown occupancy remains visible.

corrections.validation: Hazard families use distinct evidence-backed surfaces; controlled eligible Recreatiegebied Kamperland ignition affects source/adjacent fuel and occupants before unrelated areas, while coastal water follows selected defence/polder connectivity.

corrections.validation: N256 series edges never add; Zeelandbrug, Zandkreekdam/sluis bridges, Veerse Gatdam and low road sections have distinct mode/time state; closures propagate once to eligible evacuation, Mobility/Supply and Adrz access, with Unknown acceptance/throughput preserved.

Two Waterinfo observations and four forecasts through T+24 retain point/time validity only; zero local forecast coverage at T+48/T+72 is NoData.
Planned Zeelandbrug/N57/Zandkreek work is date/mode-specific lifecycle context; absent real-time confirmation is Unknown and plans cannot be applied generically to scenarios.
NWB nominal capacities are generalized scenario units; no conclusion about real bridge/dam, evacuation, care or supply throughput is supported.
Exact local hazard, affected, service, person-hour and recovery values remain synthetic until an authority-reviewed event, dynamic population and operational action ledger are bound.
